title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 247
paragraphs: This much, however, I heard from men of Cyrene, who told me they had gone to the Oracle of Ammon and had come into conversation with Etearchus king of the Ammonians; and it happened that after speaking of other matters they fell to discussing the Nile and how no one knew its sources. Etearchus said that once there had come to him men of the Nasamonians (this is a Libyan people who dwell in the Syrtis, and also in the land east of the Syrtis for no great distance), and when these Nasamonians came, and were asked by him whether they could tell him anything more than he knew about the desert parts of Libya, they said there had been among them certain sons of chief men, who were of unruly disposition; and these, when they grew up to be men, had devised various extravagant undertakings, and among them they drew lots for five of themselves to go and see the desert parts of Libya and try whether they could discover more than those who had previously explored furthest. For in the parts of Libya along the Northern Sea, beginning from Egypt and going as far as the headland of Soloeis (which is the extreme point of Libya), Libyans — and many races of them — extend along the whole coast, except such portions as the Hellenes and Phoenicians hold. But in the upper parts, which lie above the seacoast and above the peoples whose land comes down to the sea, Libya is full of wild beasts; and in the parts beyond the land of wild beasts it is full of sand, terribly waterless, and utterly desert. These young men then (they said), being sent out by their companions well supplied with water and provisions, went first through the inhabited country; after they had passed through this, they came to the country of wild beasts; and after this they passed through the desert, making their way towards the West Wind. Having crossed a great tract of sand in many days, they saw at last trees growing on a level place; and when they came up to them, they began to pluck the fruit that was on the trees. But as they began to pluck it, small men came upon them — of less stature than men of the common size — and these seized them and carried them off. Neither could the Nasamonians understand anything of their speech nor could those who were carrying them off understand the speech of the Nasamonians; and they led them (so it is said) through very great swamps, and after passing through these they came to a city in which all the men were of the same short stature as those who had carried them off, and black of skin. By the city ran a great river, which flowed from the west toward the sunrise, and in it were seen crocodiles.
